transcript.content: Hello, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Um, hi. I guess… work is kind of what pushed me to come in. I don’t mean to cause trouble or anything, but I keep getting up from my station or kind of popping up in meetings when I’m supposed to stay put.

My supervisor said it’s becoming a safety issue because I’ll just take off before I really think about it. I’m trying to do better, I really am, but it keeps happening, so… I thought I should talk to someone.
Can you tell me if you remember having similar trouble sitting still, staying focused, or acting impulsively back when you were a child or teenager?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t want to make it sound like I was, like, a bad kid or anything. But even in elementary school, I remember getting in trouble for not staying in my seat. I’d talk over the teacher without really meaning to, or blurt stuff out, and sometimes I’d just kind of wander around the room.

My mom would get notes sent home about it. I guess it was pretty similar, just… back then everyone kind of acted like I needed to try harder. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Aside from the restlessness and impulsive actions, do you also notice problems like losing focus during tasks, forgetting things, or getting easily distracted—both now and back when you were a kid?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t know if it’s as bad as the getting-up thing, but I do notice it. Like at work, when I’m doing inventory logs, I really try to pay attention, but after a few minutes the numbers kind of blur together and I realize I didn’t actually take it in, so I have to go back over it.

Same with the CNC training pages—I'll read a section and then be like, wait, what did I just read? I don’t mean to be careless. It’s just like my brain doesn’t hold onto it sometimes. Does that make sense?
Do you notice this same restlessness and trouble concentrating in other areas of your life too—like at home, when driving, or in social situations—or does it mainly happen at work?

I’m not totally sure how to answer that. I guess I notice it most at work because that’s where people point it out, you know?

At home, I don’t really have someone watching me the same way, so I don’t know if it’s as obvious. And with driving or hanging out with people… I mean, I haven’t really thought about it like that. I don’t want to say yes if I’m not sure. Does that make sense?
When you're at home relaxing or doing everyday tasks like chores, do you notice yourself getting restless, fidgety, or losing focus in a similar way to what happens at work?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but even if I’m just supposed to be standing still or sitting through something, I get this kind of… pressure in my body, like I need to move.

At work it happens by the machine or during training, but at home too, if I’m trying to stay in one place, I’ll end up pacing, stretching, or getting up to do something right then. It’s not like I’m trying to be difficult. It just feels really uncomfortable to sit still. Is that what you mean?

Would you say these same kinds of restlessness and concentration problems have been present fairly continuously all through your teens and adult life, or was there a period where they went away and then came back?

I don’t want to say it was exactly the same all through my teens, because I’m not sure I was really paying attention to it that way.

But the point where it started causing real problems was about… a year and two months ago, when I was trying to get more serious and tighten up my habits, especially moving toward the forklift and CNC certification stuff. That’s when it felt like it wasn’t just a little quirk anymore, like it was actually getting in the way.

So I guess I’d say it’s been seriously affecting me for about that long, if that answers it right.

Going back to your childhood, aside from the fidgeting and blurting out, do you also recall having trouble paying attention, following instructions, or often losing track of things like homework or toys?

Um… yeah, I guess in elementary school there were definitely signs. I don’t know if I’d say I was like, “bad” or anything, but I was the kid who had a hard time staying in my seat.

I remember talking over the teacher sometimes, blurting things out, and getting notes sent home for that kind of thing… like wandering around the room when I probably wasn’t supposed to. It’s a little embarrassing to say, but yeah, that was me. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Back in elementary school, do you remember often losing track of things like your homework, pencils, or toys, or being forgetful about daily tasks, separate from the fidgeting and blurting out?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t remember every detail from elementary school perfectly, but I do lose track of normal stuff a lot now, and I’m pretty sure that kind of forgetfulness has been around in some way.

Like at work, I’ll forget a simple step on a checklist, or forget to answer a supervisor’s text, or I’ll leave my safety glasses in my locker and then it looks like I just don’t care or I’m being careless. I don’t mean it that way at all. It’s just like those little everyday things slip out of my head.

I’m not trying to make excuses, but… yeah, I guess forgetful stuff is part of it too. Is that answering what you’re asking?
